title: SPEC still lists a pin verb the tool dropped six months ago
foundBy: session agent, while reading SPEC 3.1 for the playbook's material
details:
SPEC's host command surface lists a `pin` verb that `cs-campaign` does not have.

Section 3.1 prints `cs-campaign doctor|pin|manual|version` as the health and metadata group. Running `cs-campaign pin` answers `unknown command "pin"`, and the root command registers no such verb.

The verb was real and was removed. Commit 133ba66 replaced the operator-written pin file with the `go.mod` embedded in the binary. That change rewrote R75, deleted section 5.8 and dropped the `CS_CAMPAIGN_PIN` variable, and it left the synopsis in 3.1 naming the verb.

Two other traces are left behind. Section 7.1 lists pin among what `internal/cli` holds, which reads as the upstream check rather than a verb and is defensible. `.cs-lint.yaml` carries a `sampleSkip` waiver for `cs-campaign pin --note ...`, and no document contains that sample any more.

The surface linter has the rule that would catch this. SURF-101 refuses a command a document names and the tool lacks, and it reports zero errors here. The line is pipe-separated inside a fenced sh block, which reads as a shell pipeline rather than as four verbs.

SPEC is the contract a reader trusts about the surface. A verb listed there that does not exist is the staleness that makes the rest of the page suspect.
